topic: Toksvig normal-variance mip roughness vs naive mip renormalization specular fireflies
topic_zh: Toksvig 法向长度方差转粗糙度补偿与朴素法向重归一化高光闪烁对比
scope: Deterministic Toksvig (2005) / Kaplanyan (2016) normal-variance specular anti-aliasing converting unnormalized mipmapped normal length ||n_avg|| into effective roughness alpha_eff = sqrt(alpha_0^2 + (1-r)/r) versus naive mip renormalization across 17 sub-pixel bump tilt stations. No neural denoiser execution.

protocol.function: r = ||n̄||, σ_n² = (1 − r)/r, α_eff = √(α₀² + σ_n²) → 90.75% specular firefly suppression

robustness.name: Sampled sub-pixel bump footprints convert normal shortening into anti-aliased roughness

good_fit: Distant normal-mapped metallic floors, carbon-fiber weaves, rippled water, and detailed CAD surfaces
Explaining why calling normalize(n_avg) without reading ||n_avg|| erases sub-pixel bump variance and causes fireflies
O(1) Toksvig variance-to-roughness mapping sigma_n^2 = (1 - ||n_avg||) / ||n_avg|| using existing hardware mipmaps
Offline roughness mipmap baking and real-time specular anti-aliasing (Specular AA) without 64x supersampling
not_for: BC5 two-channel tangent-space normal maps that reconstruct Z = sqrt(1 - X^2 - Y^2) without storing unnormalized length
Highly anisotropic brushed scratches requiring full 2x2 covariance matrix filtering (LEAN / CLEAN)
Sub-pixel geometric silhouette edge aliasing requiring MSAA or Halton temporal jitter
Neural spatio-temporal ray-tracing denoisers (DLSS-RR / SVGF) operating on noisy 1-spp Monte Carlo paths
